claims.period: c1500 historical comparison; shires defined before 1300
claims.statement: Medieval nominal Dublin stretched to Wicklow town; Kildare to parts of modern Laois and Offaly; medieval Meath included Westmeath and extended toward Athlone; only Louth resembled modern county fairly closely.
A 1515 report quoted by Ellis says only half the four medieval shires was subject to king's laws, but gives no reliable percentage polygon for 1500–1509.

claims.period: 1496-08-06 appointment remains effective into 1500s subject political circumstances
claims.statement: Kildare restored to govern Ireland, appointed for 10 years and during pleasure; English Crown government substantially delegated local authority to Kildare family and alliances.
Kildare campaigned as far as Carrickfergus in 1503 and Galway in 1504. A military expedition or submission does not by itself show permanent judicial/tax control at either location.
Kildare appointed treasurer of Ireland; demonstrates crown government's official financial structure in Pale but no county-scale fiscal remittance numbers.
Kildare maintained around 300 soldiers in a standing force defending the Pale (approximate scholarly figure, not precisely dated 1504 muster).
Following 1509 accession of Henry VIII, Kildare elected justiciar by council; actual royal reappointment as deputy dated 1510-11-08, should not be incorrectly shifted into 1509.

Ellis argues English Pale government's new local defense and tillage system became financially self-sufficient: this is qualitative self-financing of Dublin administration, not proven net transfer to England.

critical_note: Historical nominal shires != present counties != effective governance; no complete geom. 1515 statement cannot become precise 50% area. No speculative net returns to English treasury.
